newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria prepares sale of Balkan Airlines - minister.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria prepares sale of Balkan Airlines - minister.

text.p: Bulgaria's Transport Minister Wilhelm Kraus said on Wednesday funding has been found for selecting a consultant for the sale of the country's indebted Balkan Airlines.
"Together with the World Bank we found a source to finance the selection of a consultant who will prepare the offer for Balkan's privatisation," Kraus told a news conference.
"Liquidation of Balkan Airlines is not a form of solving the carrier's (financial) problem. It is among the first five companies earmarked for privatisation (by the new government)," he added.
Under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund Bulgaria is to close loss-making state enterprises.
Kraus said that after the privatisation the new company could again operate as a national carrier.

He also said a compromise would be found for settling Balkan's debts to Bulgarian banks and firms for supplies of oil products, to Bulstrad insurance company, Sofia Airport and air traffic controllers.
Officials declined to specify the size of the debts.
But things are much more complicated with the airline's foreign debts, Kraus said. They include debts to firms for fuel supplies and unpaid overflight taxes.
Among the options for settling Balkan's foreign debts, suggested by the airline consultant KPMG, is consolidation of debts and an increase of the company's capital, Kraus said. He did not elaborate.
Bulgaria opened a procedure to privatise the national carrier in 1992 but in January 1995 the Privatisation Agency suspended it, citing a lack of buyers.
